extracted.intended_audience: nominating bodies, potential nominees, and administrators of the Astrid Lindgren Memorial Award
extracted.subtask_description: Regulations and criteria governing eligibility, nomination, jury composition, and administration for the Astrid Lindgren Memorial Award (a Swedish government-established prize for contributions to children’s and YA literature and reading promotion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinance (2002:1091) — fundamentals and legal basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The government determined the fundamentals for the award in an ordinance issued on December 12, 2002 (Ordinance (2002:1091) for the Astrid Lindgren Memorial Award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains instructions regarding who is eligible and what criteria the laureate must fulfill; states the award sum; states the need for a jury and an award office and outlines their functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swedish Arts Council regulations (KRFS 2014:1) — jury and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations regarding the jury, nominations and administration of the award are set out by the Swedish Arts Council in Regulations (2014:1) on the Astrid Lindgren Memorial Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies number of jury members and competence required, members’ mandate periods, the jury’s basic obligations, basic rules regarding the nomination process, and responsibilities concerning administration for the award office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury composition — twelve-member expert jury
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is evaluated by a twelve-member expert jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewarding the highest-quality work demands expert knowledge of international children’s and YA literature as well as children’s rights and children’s reading; the jury has the task of evaluating leading candidates each year and selecting a laureate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury authority over nomination rules and internal work
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury decides on the nominations and its internal work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The jury determines which bodies have the right to nominate, how many candidates each may suggest, and in which categories each group may nominate; these rules are communicated in the nomination letter sent to nominating bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination documentation and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The nomination letter to nominating bodies states what information must be included with a nomination and the deadline for submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominating bodies must follow the information and timing requirements set out in the nomination letter (details and procedural requirements are defined in that letter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipient types
rubrics_metrics.description: Laureates shall be authors, illustrators, storytellers or reading promoters, and may also be people or organizations that work to promote reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is open to individuals and organisations whose work or activity concerns children and young adults and reading promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic and spirit-based quality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Laureates must have work or activity for children and young adults that is “of the highest artistic quality” and “conveys the deeply humanistic spirit associated with Astrid Lindgren.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two phrases are core evaluative standards for selection and should guide nominators and the jury in judging candidate suitability.
